items.title: Cook Inlet LNG steps up Alaska energy push with TDI-Brooks survey
items.summary: TDI-Brooks has completed a geotechnical mission, bolstering Cook Inlet LNG’s efforts to shore up Southcentral Alaska’s energy supplies.
items.fact_excerpt:
U.S.-headquartered geotechnical and offshore survey research and service company TDI-Brooks has wrapped up a critical geotechnical campaign for Cook Inlet LNG, a strategic initiative designed to secure natural gas supplies for Southcentral Alaska, delivering vital subsurface data to support the project's anchor selection and helping bring the developer’s floating import terminal aspirations closer to reality.

TDI-Brooks has concluded a geotechnical project for the Cook Inlet LNG project (CI LNG) in Cook Inlet, Alaska, providing its Neptune N5K cone penetration testing (CPT) system for an anchor site characterization study. The work supported the project developer by collecting subsurface soil data to inform anchor selection.

According to the U.S. player, the study covered different locations within the project site with a scope of 16 CPTs in water depths ranging from 10 to 25 meters. Operations were conducted from the R/V Poseidon , a third-party vessel working in the region, demonstrating the firm’s ability to deploy specialized geotechnical equipment aboard locally available vessels.

The Cook Inlet LNG project is an energy security initiative designed to address declining natural gas reserves in the Cook Inlet basin of Southcentral Alaska to stave off a potential energy shortfall for heating and electricity by serving as a near-term bridge solution to import gas.

The completion of this study comes months after the U.S. firm was hired by Delfin LNG to provide offshore geophysical and geotechnical survey services for the Delfin deepwater port project offshore Louisiana.

source_index.title: Cook Inlet LNG steps up Alaska energy push with TDI-Brooks survey

N0.title: Cook Inlet LNG steps up Alaska energy push with TDI-Brooks survey
N0.body:
TDI-Brooks has completed a geotechnical mission, bolstering Cook Inlet LNG’s efforts to shore up Southcentral Alaska’s energy supplies.
U.S.-headquartered geotechnical and offshore survey research and service company TDI-Brooks has wrapped up a critical geotechnical campaign for Cook Inlet LNG, a strategic initiative designed to secure natural gas supplies for Southcentral Alaska, delivering vital subsurface data to support the project's anchor selection and helping bring the developer’s floating import terminal aspirations closer to reality.

TDI-Brooks has concluded a geotechnical project for the Cook Inlet LNG project (CI LNG) in Cook Inlet, Alaska, providing its Neptune N5K cone penetration testing (CPT) system for an anchor site characterization study. The work supported the project developer by collecting subsurface soil data to inform anchor selection.

According to the U.S. player, the study covered different locations within the project site with a scope of 16 CPTs in water depths ranging from 10 to 25 meters. Operations were conducted from the R/V Poseidon , a third-party vessel working in the region, demonstrating the firm’s ability to deploy specialized geotechnical equipment aboard locally available vessels.

The Cook Inlet LNG project is an energy security initiative designed to address declining natural gas reserves in the Cook Inlet basin of Southcentral Alaska to stave off a potential energy shortfall for heating and electricity by serving as a near-term bridge solution to import gas.

The completion of this study comes months after the U.S. firm was hired by Delfin LNG to provide offshore geophysical and geotechnical survey services for the Delfin deepwater port project offshore Louisiana.

items.title: Cheniere Signs Long-Term Sale and Purchase Agreements to Supply QatarEnergy with LNG through 2054
items.summary: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries,…
items.fact_excerpt:
HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere” or the “Company”) (NYSE: LNG) announced today that its subsidiaries, Sabine Pass Liquefaction, LLC (“SPL”) and Corpus Christi Liquefaction, LLC (“CCL”), have each entered into long-term liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) sale and purchase agreements (“SPA”) with QatarEnergy to supply a total of 4 million tonnes per annum (“mtpa”) of LNG through 2054.

Through Cheniere Energy Partners, L.P. (NYSE: CQP), we are developing an expansion of the existing Sabine Pass Liquefaction Project (“SPL Project”) with an expected total peak production capacity of up to approximately 20 mtpa of LNG (the “SPL Expansion Project”), inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities, which would grow the total production capacity of the SPL Project to over 50 mtpa of LNG. We expect to execute the SPL Expansion Project in a phased approach. The first phase is expected to include a single train, Train 7, and a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit, along with supporting infrastructure and tie-ins to the existing Sabine Pass LNG terminal, and has an expected total production capacity of over 6 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. In May 2026, the lump sum, turnkey engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) contract with Bechtel Energy, Inc. (“Bechtel”) for the first phase of the SPL Expansion Project was signed, and Bechtel was released to commence early engineering and procurement under a limited notice to proceed (LNTP).

items.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
items.summary: Out with hydraulics, in with electric: OneSubsea, TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron have tested all-electric tech at depths up to 3,000 meters.
items.fact_excerpt:
Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface.

OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters.

Aside from qualifying components for applications at depths of up to 3,000 meters, the project pinpointed interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies.

The company states that the completion of the project builds on more than 15 years of experience in subsea electrification and more than 5 million operating hours with electrified subsea systems.

The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

current_news.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
current_news.facts: Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface. OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters. Aside from qualifying components for applications at depths of up to 3,000 meters, the project pinpointed interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies. The company states that the completion of the project builds on more than 15 years of experience in subsea electrification and more than 5 million operating hours with electrified subsea systems. The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

Out with hydraulics, in with electric: OneSubsea, TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron have tested all-electric tech at depths up to 3,000 meters.
Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface.

OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters.

Aside from qualifying components for applications at depths of up to 3,000 meters, the project pinpointed interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies.

The company states that the completion of the project builds on more than 15 years of experience in subsea electrification and more than 5 million operating hours with electrified subsea systems.

The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

source_index.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech

N0.title: OneSubsea and oil & gas giants are unlocking deeper waters with all-electric subsea tech
N0.body:
Out with hydraulics, in with electric: OneSubsea, TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron have tested all-electric tech at depths up to 3,000 meters.
Pushing deeper into offshore frontiers, OneSubsea, a joint venture backed by SLB, Aker Solutions and Subsea7, has cleared a critical path for deepwater development through a joint industry project with France’s TotalEnergies, Norway’s Equinor, the UK’s BP, and the U.S.-headquartered Chevron to master all-electric subsea technology designed to operate 3,000 meters below the surface.

OneSubsea has completed the Brazil All-Electric Joint Industry Project (JIP) , a collaboration with TotalEnergies, Equinor, BP, and Chevron, supported through the National Petroleum Agency (ANP) research and development regulation, to advance fully electric subsea production technologies for applications at water depths of up to 3,000 meters.

Aside from qualifying components for applications at depths of up to 3,000 meters, the project pinpointed interfaces with newly developed and qualified SLB electric completion technologies.

The company states that the completion of the project builds on more than 15 years of experience in subsea electrification and more than 5 million operating hours with electrified subsea systems.

The firm’s all-electric portfolio is advancing along two complementary paths, with all-electric subsea production technology moving toward commercial deployment through Equinor’s Fram Sør project in Norway, which includes 12 all-electric subsea trees .

items.title: Over 500 piles lay the foundation for Poland’s floating LNG terminal (Gallery)
items.summary: Poland has hit a new milestone in its energy independence journey, completing the foundational piling for the new FSRU terminal in Gdańsk.
items.fact_excerpt:
Miłosz Motyka , Minister for Energy, commented: “Developing LNG infrastructure directly strengthens Poland by securing its energy supply, boosting the economy, and upgrading the country’s position across Europe. The FSRU terminal in Gdańsk will increase our capacity to import natural gas from global markets and bolster Poland’s role in the regional supply system.

“This initiative will effectively increase our gas import capacity by sea, reinforce supply diversification, and create additional opportunities for adaptable response to domestic energy demand. We remain committed to delivering investment projects that enhance the resilience and competitiveness of the Polish economy, thereby reinforcing our energy independence .”

“Nevertheless, owing to the determination of the contractors and meticulous coordination of the works, we have reached this critical milestone within the planned timeline. Now, the terminal features a robust physical foundation. Next, we will be assembling the platforms and preparing for the construction of the subsea gas pipeline .”

The work on the onshore section is also well advanced, as the Gdańsk–Gustorzyn gas pipeline underwent tests in September, which is reported to have confirmed a high standard of work and the pipeline’s good working order.

According to Gaz-System, the FSRU program is a strategic project aimed at strengthening Poland’s energy security, enabling the European country to gain an additional entry point for natural gas, increasing the diversification of supplies and system robustness.

N0.title: Over 500 piles lay the foundation for Poland’s floating LNG terminal (Gallery)
N0.body:
Poland has hit a new milestone in its energy independence journey, completing the foundational piling for the new FSRU terminal in Gdańsk.
Miłosz Motyka , Minister for Energy, commented: “Developing LNG infrastructure directly strengthens Poland by securing its energy supply, boosting the economy, and upgrading the country’s position across Europe. The FSRU terminal in Gdańsk will increase our capacity to import natural gas from global markets and bolster Poland’s role in the regional supply system.

“This initiative will effectively increase our gas import capacity by sea, reinforce supply diversification, and create additional opportunities for adaptable response to domestic energy demand. We remain committed to delivering investment projects that enhance the resilience and competitiveness of the Polish economy, thereby reinforcing our energy independence .”

“Nevertheless, owing to the determination of the contractors and meticulous coordination of the works, we have reached this critical milestone within the planned timeline. Now, the terminal features a robust physical foundation. Next, we will be assembling the platforms and preparing for the construction of the subsea gas pipeline .”

The work on the onshore section is also well advanced, as the Gdańsk–Gustorzyn gas pipeline underwent tests in September, which is reported to have confirmed a high standard of work and the pipeline’s good working order.

According to Gaz-System, the FSRU program is a strategic project aimed at strengthening Poland’s energy security, enabling the European country to gain an additional entry point for natural gas, increasing the diversification of supplies and system robustness.

items.summary: Woodside’s Scarborough, Trion, and Louisiana LNG projects have hit new milestones, with the finish line in sight for the first one.
items.fact_excerpt:
The operator emphasizes that well clean-up results are in line with reservoir and well performance expectations. The company completed all mechanical runs of Pluto Train 2 compressors, and, subsequent to the period, Scarborough gas was introduced to the warm end (gas pre-treatment) of the LNG train.

Activities in the cold end continue to progress, which will enable the start of gas liquefaction. Following the Pluto Train 1 planned major maintenance campaign in Q2, modifications to Pluto Train 1, which will allow processing of Scarborough gas, continued. The Louisiana LNG project remains on budget and was 32% complete at the end of the quarter, as LNG terminal construction advanced across marine, site works, and LNG tanks, with LNG Tank 1 wall concrete reaching 50% completion.

Currently, ongoing engagement with high-quality counterparties for equity participation and LNG offtake continues. The project is targeting the first LNG in 2029. N0.title: Australian gas project enters home stretch as developments in Mexico and US Gulf make new inroads
N0.body:
Woodside’s Scarborough, Trion, and Louisiana LNG projects have hit new milestones, with the finish line in sight for the first one.
The operator emphasizes that well clean-up results are in line with reservoir and well performance expectations. The company completed all mechanical runs of Pluto Train 2 compressors, and, subsequent to the period, Scarborough gas was introduced to the warm end (gas pre-treatment) of the LNG train.

Activities in the cold end continue to progress, which will enable the start of gas liquefaction. Following the Pluto Train 1 planned major maintenance campaign in Q2, modifications to Pluto Train 1, which will allow processing of Scarborough gas, continued. The final module arrived on-site with activities focused on module hook-up and integration. The first LNG cargo is on track for Q4 2026.

“We delivered quarterly production of 46.2 million barrels of oil equivalent, up 12% from the previous quarter following the successful completion of the Pluto LNG turnaround in the second quarter and the NWS turnaround in the third quarter.”

The Louisiana LNG project remains on budget and was 32% complete at the end of the quarter, as LNG terminal construction advanced across marine, site works, and LNG tanks, with LNG Tank 1 wall concrete reaching 50% completion.

Currently, ongoing engagement with high-quality counterparties for equity participation and LNG offtake continues. The project is targeting the first LNG in 2029. The Australian energy giant claims that structural steel supply challenges associated with ongoing disruptions in the Middle East continue to be mitigated through alternative logistics routes and fabrication sources.

items.title: Norway set on tapping into Arctic gas potential: New study to unlock 1988 Barents Sea discovery
items.summary: Norway is targeting untapped Arctic energy by commissioning a new study to shed more light on the 1988 gas discovery in the Barents Sea.
items.fact_excerpt:
Decades after being left behind in the frozen depths of the High North, a forgotten 1980s gas find in the Barents Sea is getting a second look. As Europe hungers for new energy sources and low-carbon reserves, Norway is launching a fresh push to unlock the untapped potential of the Arctic, starting with a neglected discovery 200 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle.

The Barents Sea is home to a number of discoveries that could hold vast volumes of gas but remains less explored than other parts of the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS), with several discoveries in these waters potentially containing significant volumes of gas, according to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate, which emphasizes that a new study could uncover major opportunities for one of these discoveries.

The gas discovery that this study will aim to gain more insight into is Norselhøgda (the well 7226/11-1 ), which is situated about 200 kilometers north of Hammerfest and was made in 1988. The discovery was production-tested, but the acreage was subsequently relinquished to the authorities.

Several comparable discoveries have been made in the area, which include production license 1313 , located to the north of the Norselhøgda discovery and awarded in APA 2025 . The Gro discovery in the Norwegian Sea is another discovery the Norwegian Offshore Directorate hopes to revive, along with the Linerle discovery in the Norwegian Sea.

N0.title: Norway set on tapping into Arctic gas potential: New study to unlock 1988 Barents Sea discovery
N0.body:
Norway is targeting untapped Arctic energy by commissioning a new study to shed more light on the 1988 gas discovery in the Barents Sea.
Decades after being left behind in the frozen depths of the High North, a forgotten 1980s gas find in the Barents Sea is getting a second look. As Europe hungers for new energy sources and low-carbon reserves, Norway is launching a fresh push to unlock the untapped potential of the Arctic, starting with a neglected discovery 200 kilometers north of the Arctic Circle.

The Barents Sea is home to a number of discoveries that could hold vast volumes of gas but remains less explored than other parts of the Norwegian Continental Shelf (NCS), with several discoveries in these waters potentially containing significant volumes of gas, according to the Norwegian Offshore Directorate, which emphasizes that a new study could uncover major opportunities for one of these discoveries.

The gas discovery that this study will aim to gain more insight into is Norselhøgda (the well 7226/11-1 ), which is situated about 200 kilometers north of Hammerfest and was made in 1988. The discovery was production-tested, but the acreage was subsequently relinquished to the authorities.

Several comparable discoveries have been made in the area, which include production license 1313 , located to the north of the Norselhøgda discovery and awarded in APA 2025 . The Gro discovery in the Norwegian Sea is another discovery the Norwegian Offshore Directorate hopes to revive, along with the Linerle discovery in the Norwegian Sea.

items.title: North Sea gas field cleared for take-off: UK greenlights Jackdaw after legal storms
items.summary: The UK regulator has given Shell-backed Adura the go-ahead for a North Sea gas field following a courtroom showdown with environmental campaigners.
items.fact_excerpt:
Jackdaw has the potential to deliver around 6% of projected UK North Sea gas production, which is considered to be enough fuel to heat the equivalent of 1.4 million homes at a time when older gas fields are reaching the end of their production.

The field, located approximately 250 kilometers east of Aberdeen, is expected to be among the lowest-emission developments on the UK Continental Shelf (UKCS), while supporting jobs and bolstering Britain’s energy security.

The field is located in the Central North Sea (CNS), 30 kilometers southeast of the Shearwater platform and adjacent to the UK/Norway median line. Jackdaw is a gas/condensate development comprising a not permanently attended wellhead platform with four wells, tied back to the Shearwater hub via a 31-kilometer pipeline.

While the latest approval marks a major turning point, the environmental battles are not entirely over since environmental groups like Greenpeace remain strongly opposed to the development of the North Sea oil and gas projects, which have become a primary battleground for climate litigation.

Responding to the government giving the Jackdaw gas field the go-ahead, Sam Richards , CEO of Britain Remade, said: “Britain is going to need gas for decades to come, as even the Climate Change Committee recognises. The choice is not between gas and no gas, but between gas produced in British waters and gas shipped in from abroad at higher cost and with higher emissions.

The field is located in the Central North Sea (CNS), 30 kilometers southeast of the Shearwater platform and adjacent to the UK/Norway median line. items.title: LNG Canada entrusts Técnicas Reunidas with €200M+ EPCM deal
items.summary: Técnicas Reunidas has secured work on LNG Canada's Coastal GasLink Phase 2, fueling the engineering firm's North American growth.
items.fact_excerpt:
Técnicas Reunidas, a Spanish-based engineering contractor, is cementing its footprint in North America, with an engineering, procurement and construction management (EPCM) assignment worth more than €200 million for Phase 2 of the Coastal GasLink pipeline awarded by LNG Canada, a joint venture featuring Shell, Petronas, PetroChina, Mitsubishi Corporation, and KOGAS.

CGL Phase 2 will be delivered through an integrated execution model, with LNG Canada leading project construction as Phase 2 Execution Manager and TR Canada E&C providing the EPCM services, while CGL will remain the owner, operator, and permit holder of the pipeline and associated facilities.

The contract award comes only weeks after LNG Canada reached its Phase 2 final investment decision (FID) to advance the next stage of development of this British Columbia-based project of national significance.

The project includes the construction of five additional compressor stations, as well as modifications to both existing and planned facilities at various points along the pipeline route.

The newly awarded contract with LNG Canada adds to the company’s extensive experience in midstream projects, which includes 30,000 kilometers of oil and gas pipelines and more than 35 large compression projects worldwide.

items.title: FERC comes up with three-tiered fast track plan to streamline US LNG permitting
items.summary: FERC has proposed an LNG blanket authorization program to slash red tape, optimize permitting, and fast-track U.S. energy infrastructure development.
items.fact_excerpt:
FERC’s notice of proposed rulemaking (NOPR) intends to establish an LNG blanket authorization program to allow eligible activities at LNG facilities to proceed without case-specific authorization orders under Sections 3 and 7 of the Natural Gas Act (NGA). This program is modeled on the commission’s 40-year blanket certificate program for interstate natural gas pipelines.

Laura V. Swett , FERC’s Chairman, commented: “American energy dominance requires us to build and maintain the energy infrastructure our country needs without unnecessary delay. I am immensely proud of FERC’s historic proposal.

Under the automatic authorization umbrella are activities that would not increase an LNG plant’s authorized capacity, expand the authorized vertical or horizontal extents within the plant’s footprint, or cause flows, levels, volumes, pressures, temperatures, compositions, or loads to exceed applicable design limits.

A 60-day prior notice covers activities that may increase the plant’s authorized capacity but remain within the plant’s footprint and do not cause operating conditions to exceed the design limits of the affected or remaining facilities.

A 90-day prior notice entails construction of new LNG facilities, such as liquefaction trains, LNG tanks, and marine berths, and related auxiliary systems, including those located outside the plant’s footprint, subject to limitations on facility type, location, and size.

items.title: Timor-Leste throws 12-month lifeline to delayed gas project ahead of drilling ops
items.summary: This extension for a gas field in Timor-Leste follows earlier termination warnings as partnership talks and drilling preparations press ahead.
items.fact_excerpt:
October 20, 2026 · 2 days ago

SundaGas Banda Unipessoal, a wholly owned subsidiary of the UK-based and AIM-listed Sunda Energy, has dodged a bullet in Timor-Leste with a crucial 12-month reprieve, since the regulatory extension keeps hopes alive for the long-awaited appraisal well following a termination warning earlier this year over missed deadlines, as partner negotiations heat up.

Sunda Energy’s subsidiary has received from Autoridade Nacional do Petróleo (ANP), Timor-Leste’s upstream regulator, an extension of 12 months to the current phase of the production sharing contract (PSC) TL-SO-19-16, which contains the Chuditch gas field, where SundaGas has been preparing to drill the Chuditch-2 appraisal well. The firm operates this asset in partnership with its government-owned joint venture partner, Timor Gap Chuditch Unipessoal .

The extension granted by ANP allows the joint venture time to continue the discussions, with a stated timeline for completion prior to the end of 2026. Sunda explains that this extension is subject to a suspension of the uplift on the cost recovery account for the PSC from June 19, 2024, until such time as drilling operations on Chuditch-2 have started.

The firm is continuing to liaise with Finder under the framework of the letter of intent announced in April 2026 with respect to collaboration between the planned drilling campaigns for KTJ and Chuditch-2 drilling campaigns.

items.title: United Oil & Gas eyes billion-barrel Jamaican drilling targets as it maps out next steps
items.summary: United Oil & Gas has unveiled new rig and logistics study results for its license offshore Jamaica, boosting ongoing farm-out talks.
items.fact_excerpt:
October 20, 2026 · 2 days ago

United Oil & Gas has unveiled new rig and logistics study results for its license offshore Jamaica, boosting ongoing farm-out talks.

Brian Larkin , Chief Executive Officer, commented: “The completion of this study is an important step forward for the Walton-Morant license. It supports our ongoing farmout process, providing practical insight into rig and equipment availability and critical path items required to access the greater than 1 billion barrel mean prospective resources contained within Colibri and Thunderball, representing two targets within our portfolio of 40 leads and prospects containing over 7.2 billion barrels of prospective resources.

The assessment covers Colibri , in approximately 750 meters water depth, and Thunderball , a potential follow-on well in approximately 1,900 meters water depth. Colibri has a mean prospective resource of 406 million barrels of oil, while Thunderball has a mean prospective resource of 603 million barrels of oil and forms part of a wider series of large, tilted fault-block structures in the Morant Basin.

The AIM-listed player underlined: “This study is a forward-planning and market assessment review and does not constitute a commitment, at this time, by United to drill a well.

items.title: Eni and Libya’s National Oil Corporation turning on the taps at African gas project
items.summary: This gas project is set to slash 1.5 million tonnes of annual carbon emissions while unlocking fresh energy supplies for a growing domestic grid.
items.fact_excerpt:
This gas project is set to slash 1.5 million tonnes of annual carbon emissions while unlocking fresh energy supplies for a growing domestic grid.

A gas project off the coast of Libya, which is operated by Mellitah Oil & Gas Libyan Branch, a consortium formed by National Oil Corporation (NOC) of Libya and Eni North Africa, is anticipated to stop decades of costly flaring in its tracks, capturing hundreds of millions of cubic meters of gas to fuel local power plants and feed European export pipelines.

The recovered gas will be supplied to the domestic market, providing an incremental production of around 700 million standard cubic meters per year, helping meet demand from the power generation sector.

In addition, the project will support additional gas volumes available for export to Europe through the GreenStream pipeline. Saipem finished the lifting operations of the gas recovery module for the BGUP earlier this year.

The pre-commissioning activities were planned for approximately 28 kilometers of already laid subsea pipelines to connect the DP3, DP4, and Sabratha platforms to enable the transportation of the recovered gas to the Mellitah treatment complex.

items.title: Petronas and Petrovietnam strengthen ties in pursuit of energy security and low-carbon growth
items.summary: Petronas and Petrovietnam are expanding their 35-year partnership across LNG, upstream development, and low-carbon energy arsenal in Vietnam.
items.fact_excerpt:
October 19, 2026 · 3 days ago

Petronas and Petrovietnam are expanding their 35-year partnership across LNG, upstream development, and low-carbon energy arsenal in Vietnam.

Asian energy giants Malaysia's Petronas and Vietnam National Industry – Energy Group (Petrovietnam) have forged a strategic alliance agreement (SAA) to supercharge Vietnam's energy security, expand liquefied natural gas (LNG) infrastructure, and accelerate low-carbon solutions across the region.

This agreement establishes a forward-looking framework for both organizations to leverage their respective strengths and pursue opportunities across the energy value chain, spanning upstream development, gas and LNG, and downstream opportunities, as well as low-carbon solutions.

Petronas has been present in Vietnam since 1991, when it made its first investment in the country’s upstream sector as a pioneer international investor in Vietnam’s oil and gas industry.

items.title: Nordic energy players hit paydirt with new gas and condensate discovery
items.summary: Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels.
items.fact_excerpt:
Vår Energi and Equinor have struck gas and condensate in Norwegian waters, packing up to 5.5 million barrels.

Norway’s energy duo, Vår Energi and Equinor, have made a gas and condensate find in a new Norwegian Sea license, uncovering a fresh prospect estimated to hold up to 5.5 million barrels of oil equivalent (boe).

Vår Energi and Equinor have made a gas and condensate discovery in the 6407/5-3 S well, which is known as the Lakris prospect in the Gimsan Basin on the Halten Terrace in the Norwegian Sea.

The water depth at the site is 218 meters. The well, which was not formation-tested, but data and samples were collected, will now be permanently plugged and abandoned.

The well 6407/5-3 S encountered gas and condensate in the upper Tilje Formation in heterolithic reservoir rocks, totalling 54 meters, with moderate to poor reservoir quality. The gas/water contact was not encountered in the well.

items.title: Completing electrification project at Troll
items.summary: The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year.
items.fact_excerpt:
The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The Troll field continues to deliver high and stable production of oil and gas to Europe with low emissions.

The Troll licence partnership has informed the Norwegian Ministry of Energy that the Troll West Electrification (TWEL) project will be completed after commissioning the first electric export compressor on Troll C, and without installing the second electric export compressor on Troll C, as originally planned in the 2021 plan for development and operation (PDO).

The decision also helps maintain high and stable gas supplies to Europe at a time when energy security remains important. It is expected to make around 2.3 billion standard cubic metres of additional gas available to the European market in 2027 and 2028. This corresponds to approximately two years of gas consumption for around one million European households.

Troll A became the first platform on the Norwegian continental shelf to receive power from shore in 1996. Troll B and Troll C were partially electrified in 2024. TWEL has reduced emissions from the Troll area by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year, corresponding to approximately 75% of the emission reductions originally planned in the PDO (440,000 tonnes per year). This makes the project one of the largest emissions reduction measures on the Norwegian continental shelf. Overall, the measures have reduced emissions from the Troll area to approximately the same level as in 1999.

items.title: Oil and gas discovery in the North Sea adding volumes to Oseberg
items.summary: Equinor and its partners Petoro and TotalEnergies have made an oil and gas discovery in exploration well 30/8-7 S Grimsnes near the Oseberg field.
items.fact_excerpt:
Norwegian oil and gas are essential to European energy security. Norway covers 20% of Europe's oil needs and 30% of its gas needs, but production from existing fields is declining as they mature.

Maintaining high activity levels and reliable energy supplies to Europe will require continued exploration and development of marginal discoveries near existing infrastructure. Towards 2035, Equinor plans to drill 200 near-field exploration wells and deliver around 75 subsea developments.

“To bring these discoveries on stream, we must radically change how we plan and develop subsea projects. Our aim is to halve both costs and the time from discovery to production through simpler and faster processes, more standardisation, repeatable solutions and more extensive use of industry standards. We expect the partnership to make an investment decision for Grimsnes as early as next summer, with production within three years,” says Gunnar Nakken”, senior vice president for projects and subsea on the Norwegian continental shelf.

Equinor's ambition is to maintain production of 1.3 million barrels of oil equivalent per day on the Norwegian continental shelf in 2035. Around 70% of this will come from new wells and developments.

The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The Troll field continues to deliver high and stable production of oil and gas to Europe with low emissions.

items.title: Mixed outlook for energy expenditures this winter
items.summary: We expect energy expenditures this winter to vary because of diverging trends in energy prices among fuels and regional variation in forecast temperatures. We expect that lower prices for natural gas and propane will drive decreases in expenditures this year for the half of U.S. households heating with those fuels. items.title: U.S. LNG exports rose 23% in the first half of 2026 because of higher capacity
items.summary: U.S. liquefied natural gas (LNG) exports averaged 17.4 billion cubic feet per day (Bcf/d) in the first six months of the year, 23% more than the same period in 2025, according to our Natural Gas Monthly. In our latest Short-Term Energy Outlook, we estimate U.S. LNG exports will average 17.3 Bcf/d in the second half of 2026 (2H26) before rising to 18.7 Bcf/d in 1H27.

items.title: New England natural gas prices have been trading near record discounts to Henry Hub
items.summary: Low-cost Appalachian and Canadian natural gas supplies coupled with lower-than-usual regional consumption have pushed down natural gas prices at a major New England pricing hub in recent months to trade at a discount to the widely cited U.S. benchmark, Henry Hub.

items.title: Corpus Christi LNG expansion makes facility the second-largest in the United States
items.summary: On August 28, 2026, Cheniere Energy, Inc., completed its Corpus Christi Liquefaction Stage 3 Project (CCL Stage 3) in Texas, taking custody and control of the seventh and last liquefied natural gas (LNG) train in the project.

items.title: Public companies produce most U.S. crude oil and natural gas
items.summary: Publicly traded companies represent a tiny share of the total number of companies producing crude oil and natural gas in the United States, but they make up a large share of U.S. production. In 2025, publicly traded companies accounted for just 2% of about 12,000 oil and natural gas producers but produced 68% of the crude oil and natural gas in the Lower 48 states.

items.title: Henry Hub natural gas prices this summer were 6% lower than last summer
items.summary: The Henry Hub natural gas spot price averaged $2.93 per million British thermal units from June through August, 6% less than the same period last year. Prices were lower this summer despite exceptionally hot weather that increased electricity demand for air conditioning. Natural gas-fired power plants often help meet higher demand during such periods.

items.title: U.S. natural gas production reached a record high in July 2026
items.summary: U.S. natural gas production hit an all-time high in July 2026, driven primarily by increased output in the Permian Basin, according to our latest Natural Gas Monthly.

items.title: EIG’s MidOcean Energy lines up new investment as NYK spreads its LNG wings
items.summary: MidOcean Energy, a liquefied natural gas (LNG) player formed and managed by the U.S.-headquartered investment company EIG Global Energy Partners (EIG), has secured another investment, which enables Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK), Japan’s shipping and logistics major, to widen its LNG footprint.
items.fact_excerpt:
MidOcean Energy, a liquefied natural gas (LNG) player formed and managed by the U.S.-headquartered investment company EIG Global Energy Partners (EIG), has secured another investment, enabling Nippon Yusen Kabushiki Kaisha (NYK), Japan’s shipping and logistics major, to widen its LNG footprint.

Following the investment, Diamond Gas MidOcean is expected to be operated as a jointly owned company by Mitsubishi Corporation and NYK. In addition, the Japanese giant plans to enter into a strategic partnership with MidOcean Energy. The collaboration’s focus is on LNG marine transportation.

The share subscription is subject to the receipt of competition law and other required regulatory approvals from the relevant authorities. The completion is expected to occur between August and September 2026. This investment represents NYK’s continued expansion along the LNG value chain.

Previously, the company made investments in the Wheatstone LNG and Cameron LNG projects, as well as in LNG-fueled vessel transportation and LNG bunkering businesses, as part of its growth strategy set out in its medium-term management plan .

Before this, EIG’s LNG arm revealed a $120 million equity investment from The Arab Energy Fund, shortly after Tokyo-based Idemitsu Kosan decided to pour $500 million , followed by Shizuoka Gas’ intention to invest $100 million in the LNG company.

items.title: Floating wind turbine that will power UK gas platform ready for tow to offshore site
items.summary: The Culzean floating wind turbine, which will supply electricity to the Culzean gas platform in the North Sea, off the coast of Scotland, will soon be towed to its offshore location as the integration of the wind turbine with the floating foundation has been completed. Archer, the engineering, procu
items.fact_excerpt:
The Culzean floating wind turbine, which will supply electricity to the Culzean gas platform in the North Sea, off the coast of Scotland, will soon be towed to its offshore location as the integration of the wind turbine with the floating foundation has been completed.

The floating wind pilot was one of the 13 Innovation and Targeted Oil & Gas (INTOG) offshore wind projects awarded seabed rights by Crown Estate Scotland in 2023, with TotalEnergies, the operator of the Culzean gas field, being the company that secured the rights.

Currently, the Culzean Floating Wind project is being led by NEO NEXT+ Energy, an independent UK oil and gas producer formed on March 30, 2026, through the merger of NEO Energy, Repsol UK, and TotalEnergies’ UK upstream business.

Once commissioned, the turbine is expected to provide about 20% of the platform’s electricity demand, reducing greenhouse gas emissions by supplementing power currently generated by gas turbines.

Besides supplying renewable power to the gas platform, the Culzean Floating Wind pilot is planned to serve as a demonstration platform for floating wind technology, generating operational data and experience to support future commercial projects. The semi-submersible foundation has been designed for modular fabrication and is optimized for rapid assembly, according to Ocergy, for which the project marks the first commercial deployment of its OCG-Wind floating foundation technology.

items.title: Canada: Allseas to install critical subsea section of remote natural gas pipeline
items.summary: Allseas has secured a contract with Western LNG to install the critical subsea section of the Prince Rupert Gas Transmission (PRGT) pipeline in Canada. Located in the remote waters of north-western British Columbia, near the Alaska border, the subsea pipeline forms the final link in the 700-kilomete
items.fact_excerpt:
Allseas has secured a contract with Western LNG to install the critical subsea section of the Prince Rupert Gas Transmission (PRGT) pipeline in Canada.

Located in the remote waters of north-western British Columbia, near the Alaska border, the subsea pipeline forms the final link in the 700-kilometer system transporting Canadian natural gas to the planned Ksi Lisims LNG export facility on the Pacific coast..

Allseas ’ scope comprises approximately 50 kilometers of 36- and 48-inch concrete-weight-coated pipeline, connecting the onshore transmission system to the planned floating LNG facility on Pearse Island.

Ksi Lisims LNG is a proposed 12 mtpa floating export facility being developed by the Nisga’a Nation, Rockies LNG, and Western LNG. The project will be situated on Nisga’a Nation-owned land, a strategically located site with direct and efficient routes to growing Asian markets.

The project and its feed pipeline PRGT have received key environmental approvals and have been identified as projects of national interest by the Canadian government. Pending a final investment decision (FID) by the project co-developers, construction could begin by early 2027.

items.fact_excerpt:
The Western Australian Government has granted State Significant Project status to a Woodside Energy-operated offshore development project, described as Australia’s largest untapped conventional gas resource.

With a forecast production capacity of 11.4 MTPA and a peak condensate production rate of 50,000 barrels per day, the proposed Browse to North West Shelf (NWS) Project would deliver natural gas from the Calliance, Torosa, and Brecknock fields to the existing Karratha gas plant via an approximately 900-kilometer pipeline, connected to two floating production, storage, and offloading (FPSO) units.

A carbon capture and storage (CCS) solution has been incorporated into the project design and is expected to enable a reduction of 53 million tons (mt) CO2e of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions as compared to the project’s 2019 Scope 1 emissions estimate.

According to Woodside Energy, State Significant Project status represents the highest level of prioritization available under the Western Australian Government’s Lead Agency Framework, which is designed to guide proponents through the approvals process. It will support coordinated engagement as the project progresses towards key approvals and development milestones.

An independent economic impact assessment indicates the project could deliver a long-term uplift of around A$141 billion in gross domestic product nationally and approximately A$56 billion in taxes and royalties, including around A$19.8 billion in petroleum resource rent tax.

N0.title: Australia’s ‘largest untapped’ conventional gas resource gets significant project status
N0.body:
The Western Australian Government has granted State Significant Project status to a Woodside Energy-operated offshore development project, described as Australia’s largest untapped conventional gas resource. With a forecast production capacity of 11.4 MTPA and a peak condensate production rate of 50
The Western Australian Government has granted State Significant Project status to a Woodside Energy-operated offshore development project, described as Australia’s largest untapped conventional gas resource.

With a forecast production capacity of 11.4 MTPA and a peak condensate production rate of 50,000 barrels per day, the proposed Browse to North West Shelf (NWS) Project would deliver natural gas from the Calliance, Torosa, and Brecknock fields to the existing Karratha gas plant via an approximately 900-kilometer pipeline, connected to two floating production, storage, and offloading (FPSO) units.

A carbon capture and storage (CCS) solution has been incorporated into the project design and is expected to enable a reduction of 53 million tons (mt) CO2e of greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions as compared to the project’s 2019 Scope 1 emissions estimate.

According to Woodside Energy, State Significant Project status represents the highest level of prioritization available under the Western Australian Government’s Lead Agency Framework, which is designed to guide proponents through the approvals process. It will support coordinated engagement as the project progresses towards key approvals and development milestones.

An independent economic impact assessment indicates the project could deliver a long-term uplift of around A$141 billion in gross domestic product nationally and approximately A$56 billion in taxes and royalties, including around A$19.8 billion in petroleum resource rent tax.

items.fact_excerpt:
Dutch gas infrastructure company Gasunie has launched a public tender seeking a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) from a new-build offshore wind farm as part of its target to source 40% of its energy from carbon-free sources by 2030.

The electricity must be physically delivered together with the associated and traceable Guarantees of Origin (GoOs), according to the contract notice published in the Supplement to the Official Journal of the European Union on July 24.

The procurement also includes two optional capacity increases. The first would add 10 MW from 2029/2030 until 2036, potentially extending until the end of the contract, subject to a final investment decision (FID) on the EemsEnergyTerminal project in the first half of 2027.

The LNG import terminal in Eemshaven has been operational since September 2022 and was originally contracted for a period of five years. In June this year, Gasunie and its partner Vopak took a conditional investment decision (cFID) on extending the operations of the LNG terminal beyond 2027.

The deadline for bids expires at 11:00 CET on September 30, 2026, while requests for additional information can be made until September 4, 2026.

N0.title: Gasunie launches tender for 10-year offshore wind PPA in Netherlands
N0.body:
Dutch gas infrastructure company Gasunie has launched a public tender seeking a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) from a new-build offshore wind farm as part of its target to source 40% of its energy from carbon-free sources by 2030. Through the tender, Gasunie is seeking to procure 40 MW of
Dutch gas infrastructure company Gasunie has launched a public tender seeking a long-term power purchase agreement (PPA) from a new-build offshore wind farm as part of its target to source 40% of its energy from carbon-free sources by 2030.

The electricity must be physically delivered together with the associated and traceable Guarantees of Origin (GoOs), according to the contract notice published in the Supplement to the Official Journal of the European Union on July 24.

The procurement also includes two optional capacity increases. The first would add 10 MW from 2029/2030 until 2036, potentially extending until the end of the contract, subject to a final investment decision (FID) on the EemsEnergyTerminal project in the first half of 2027.

The LNG import terminal in Eemshaven has been operational since September 2022 and was originally contracted for a period of five years. In June this year, Gasunie and its partner Vopak took a conditional investment decision (cFID) on extending the operations of the LNG terminal beyond 2027.

The deadline for bids expires at 11:00 CET on September 30, 2026, while requests for additional information can be made until September 4, 2026.

items.title: Equinor and Uniper sign 15-year gas sales agreement for supplies to Germany
items.summary: Equinor and the energy company Uniper have signed a 15-year agreement for supplies of natural gas to Germany.
items.fact_excerpt:
Equinor and the energy company Uniper have signed a 15-year agreement for supplies of natural gas to Germany. Under the agreement, Equinor will deliver more than 30 TWh (ca. 2.8 billion cubic metres) of natural gas per year to Uniper.

Supplies under the new agreement will be from 1 January 2027 to 31 December 2041 with the gas delivered at Trading Hub Europe, the German gas market area. Pricing will reflect market terms, while other commercial details are confidential between the parties.

“We are pleased to extend our long-standing partnership with Uniper. This agreement demonstrates the strong demand for reliable, long-term gas supplies from the Norwegian continental shelf, which delivers energy and industrial feedstock with a lower carbon footprint than alternative gas supply. It further strengthens Equinor’s role as a trusted long-term energy partner to Europe, says Anders Opedal, president and CEO of Equinor.

Germany is Equinor’s largest market for natural gas and has been an anchor market for Norwegian gas since exports started in 1977. Deliveries under the new agreement will start on 1 January 2027, the same year Norway and Equinor mark 50 years of gas exports to Germany.

Natural gas is expected to remain a key part of Europe’s future energy mix, supporting security of supply, industrial activity and flexibility in the energy system as more renewable power and low-carbon gases are developed.

items.title: Equinor and Eneco sign five-year gas agreement with verified emissions data
items.summary: Equinor and Dutch energy company Eneco have signed a five-year agreement for natural gas deliveries.
items.fact_excerpt:
Equinor and Dutch energy company Eneco have signed a five-year agreement for natural gas deliveries. The covers around 9 TWh of natural gas per year, or approximately 0.9 billion cubic metres, to the Dutch gas grid with deliveries started on 1 October 2026.

The agreement covers gas from the Norwegian continental shelf, where production and pipeline transport have a comparatively low greenhouse gas footprint among gas sources supplied to Europe. Commercial terms are confidential between the parties.

In addition to the gas supply, Equinor will transfer verified environmental attributes to Eneco through the digital platform operated by Attributes SA. The greenhouse gas footprint of the gas under this contract is 11.8% lower * than the average for gas supplied through the Dutch grid.

*The calculation of the CO2e footprint is based on total lifecycle emissions (extraction, transport, combustion) using emission factors from CO2-emissiefactoren.nl . This is the Dutch standard for CO₂ calculations, for which Royal Haskoning performs the underlying lifecycle emission calculations for natural gas. The difference between the Dutch natural gas mix and the gas supplied by Equinor is determined annually. The current comparison is based on 2025. There is no difference in emissions during gas consumption, but there is a difference regarding the extraction and transport of the Norwegian gas.

Equinor's long-term safety trend is stable at the end of the third quarter of 2026. There have been no incidents with major accident potential or serious well control incidents in the quarter.

items.summary: Equinor and its partners have discovered gas at the Gullfaks South field, 190 kilometres northwest of Bergen.
items.fact_excerpt:
Equinor and its partners have discovered gas at the Gullfaks South field, 190 kilometres northwest of Bergen.

Between 0.5 million and 1.6 million standard cubic metres of recoverable oil equivalents have been discovered. This corresponds to 3.3 to 10.3 million barrels of oil equivalent.

The exploration well is formally named 34/10-D-4 BH.

items.title: Updated cost estimate for the Snøhvit Future project
items.summary: On behalf of the partnership, Equinor has updated the cost estimate for Snøhvit Future to NOK 26.5 billion in 2026 value.
items.fact_excerpt:
On behalf of the partnership, Equinor has updated the cost estimate for Snøhvit Future to NOK 26.5 billion in 2026 value. The timetable for the project remains unchanged, with onshore compression planned to start in 2029 and electrification in 2030.

"We have worked closely with the suppliers to manage the complexity of the project and work together every day to deliver the project safely and efficiently. Snøhvit Future is still a profitable project that supports jobs in Hammerfest, Norwegian value creation and energy supply to Europe towards 2050," says Bokn.

The project serves two purposes. Onshore compression will help maintain plateau production at Hammerfest LNG when reservoir pressure declines. Electrification of Hammerfest LNG will cut annual CO₂ emissions by 850,000 tonnes, equivalent to two per cent of Norway's annual emissions.

Snøhvit Future is about 60 per cent complete. The compressor module was installed in August, and there is a high level of activity at Melkøya, in the tunnel project and among suppliers. In the development phase, it is expected that more than 70 per cent of value creation will go to Norwegian companies. More than a third of this will go to Northern Norway.

The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The Troll field continues to deliver high and stable production of oil and gas to Europe with low emissions.

items.title: More gas for 30-year-old Troll A
items.summary: The Troll A platform in the North Sea is being supplied with additional gas. On 22 August production started from the Troll Phase 3 stage 2 subsea project.
items.fact_excerpt:
The Troll A platform in the North Sea is being supplied with additional gas. On 22 August production started from the Troll Phase 3 stage 2 subsea project.

This helps maintain jobs, value creation and high gas deliveries to Europe from Troll A and the Kollsnes processing plant, which marks its 30th anniversary this year.

"Troll is the backbone of Norwegian gas exports to Europe. This project accelerates production from the reservoir, helping maintain today’s high level of gas exports from Troll and Kollsnes for as long as possible. With both Troll A and the Kollsnes gas plant powered by electricity from shore, the gas is produced with very low emissions," says Lill Harriet Brusdal, vice president for Troll and Kvitebjørn.

“We start production with excellent HSE results, ahead of schedule and several hundred million Norwegian kroner below the cost estimate. The main reasons are efficient marine operations and a highly efficient drilling campaign, which was completed 25 per cent faster than planned," says Trond Bokn, senior vice president for project development in Equinor.

In this way, the project has generated significant ripple effects in Norway. In operations it helps maintain secure gas deliveries to Europe, jobs and revenues for society. More than 90 per cent of the profits from the Troll field go to the state through taxes and direct ownership in the field via Petoro.

items.title: Expanding Troll: more gas to Europe
items.summary: Equinor and its partners are investing just over NOK 4 billion in a new subsea development that will increase gas production from the Troll field.
items.fact_excerpt:
Equinor and its partners Petoro, Shell, TotalEnergies og ConocoPhillips are investing just over NOK 4 billion in a new subsea development that will increase gas production from the Troll field in the North Sea.

“We have an ambition to start production as early as 2028. By simplifying, increasing standardisation and reusing existing infrastructure and equipment, we are reducing costs and enabling faster production, in line with our new ways of working. The project helps sustain jobs, value creation and secure gas exports to Europe from Troll A and Kollsnes,” says Gunnar Nakken, senior vice president for projects and subsea Norway in Equinor.

The TWIN project is expected to contribute around 11 billion standard cubic metres of gas. It is the third step of Troll phase 3, which produces gas from the Troll West reservoir.

This is one of many subsea projects planned on the Norwegian continental shelf in the coming years. Both the industry and the authorities are focused on simplifying processes, reducing costs and bringing new volumes on stream more quickly.

The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The Troll field continues to deliver high and stable production of oil and gas to Europe with low emissions.

items.title: 5,000 oil cargoes from Gullfaks
items.summary: Oil cargo number 5,000 has been delivered from the Gullfaks field in the North Sea.
items.fact_excerpt:
Oil cargo number 5,000 has been delivered from the Gullfaks field in the North Sea. The milestone demonstrates how continued development of mature fields on the Norwegian continental shelf supports stable energy supply to Europe at a time marked by increasing geopolitical unrest.

When production started in 1986, the field was expected to produce until 2007. Two decades later, weekly oil cargoes are still shipped to the international market, with most volumes going to Europe. In total, Gullfaks has produced around 2.8 billion barrels of oil equivalent – nearly twice as much as originally estimated. The field also serves as an export hub for oil from the Snorre and Visund fields, as well as several subsea developments in the area.

The oil is transported by shuttle tankers – specialised vessels with a cargo capacity of around 800,000 barrels of crude oil – providing flexible and reliable transport between the Norwegian continental shelf and European customers.

Oil cargo number 5,000 was delivered to St1’s refinery in Gothenburg, which produces fuels such as gasoline, jet fuel, diesel and marine fuels. These products are distributed through around 1,150 retail sites in Finland, Sweden and Norway. Gullfaks crude is also delivered to refineries in the UK and Poland, and occasionally to Equinor’s own refinery at Mongstad.

The partial electrification of Troll B and Troll C has reduced emissions by around 330,000 tonnes of CO₂ per year. The Troll field continues to deliver high and stable production of oil and gas to Europe with low emissions.

items.title: Cheniere Declares Quarterly Dividend
items.summary: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere”) (NYSE: LNG) today announced that its Board of Directors has…
items.fact_excerpt:
HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Cheniere Energy, Inc. (“Cheniere”) (NYSE: LNG) today announced that its Board of Directors has declared a quarterly cash dividend of $0.555 per common share payable on May 19, 2026 to shareholders of record as of the close of business on May 11, 2026.

Cheniere Energy, Inc. is the leading producer and exporter of liquefied natural gas (“LNG”) in the United States, reliably providing a clean, secure, and affordable solution to the growing global need for natural gas. Cheniere is a full-service LNG provider, with capabilities that include gas procurement and transportation, liquefaction, vessel chartering, and LNG delivery. Cheniere has one of the largest liquefaction platforms in the world, consisting of the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi liquefaction facilities on the U.S. Gulf Coast, with total production capacity of over 53 million tonnes per annum (“mtpa”) of LNG in operation and an additional approximately 8 mtpa of expected production capacity under construction. Cheniere is also pursuing liquefaction expansion opportunities and other projects along the LNG value chain. Cheniere is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and has additional offices in London, Singapore, Beijing, Tokyo, Dubai and Washington, D.C.

For additional information, please refer to the Cheniere website at www.cheniere.com and Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025, filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

items.fact_excerpt:
Substantially all of the derivative gains (losses) relate to the use of commodity derivative instruments indexed to international gas and LNG prices, primarily related to our long-term IPM agreements. Our IPM agreements are designed to provide stable margins on purchases of natural gas and sales of LNG over the life of the agreements and have a fixed fee component, similar to that of LNG sold under our long-term, fixed fee LNG sale and purchase agreements. However, the long-term duration and international price basis of our IPM agreements make them particularly susceptible to fluctuations in fair market value from period to period. In addition, accounting requirements prescribe recognition of these long-term gas supply agreements at the fair value each reporting period on a mark-to-market basis, but do not currently permit mark-to-market recognition of the corresponding sale of LNG, resulting in a mismatch of accounting recognition for the purchase of natural gas and sale of LNG. As a result of increased international gas price volatility and increases in international forward commodity curves during the three months ended March 31, 2026, we recognized $5.4 billion of non-cash unfavorable changes in the fair value attributable to such positions (before tax and non-controlling interests), compared to $219 million of non-cash unfavorable changes in fair value in the corresponding 2025 period.

As of May 1, 2026, over 4,760 cumulative LNG cargoes totaling over 325 million tonnes of LNG have been produced, loaded and exported from our liquefaction projects.

Through Cheniere Partners, we are developing an expansion adjacent to the SPL Project with an expected total peak production capacity of up to approximately 20 mtpa of LNG (the “SPL Expansion Project”), inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities. We expect to execute the SPL Expansion Project in a phased approach, and a positive Final Investment Decision (“FID”) is subject to, among other things, receipt of necessary regulatory approvals and acceptable commercial and financing arrangements. The FERC application for authorization to site, construct and operate the SPL Expansion Project, as well as the Department of Energy (“DOE”) application authorizing the export of LNG to non-free trade agreement (“FTA”) countries, remain pending. In May 2026, the lump sum, turnkey EPC contract with Bechtel for the first phase of the SPL Expansion Project was signed, and Bechtel was released to commence early engineering and procurement under a LNTP. The first phase includes a single train, Train 7, and a boil-off gas re-liquefaction unit, along with supporting infrastructure and tie-ins to the existing Sabine Pass LNG terminal, and has an expected total production capacity of over 6 mtpa of LNG, inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities.

We are constructing an expansion adjacent to the CCL Stage 3 Project consisting of two additional Midscale Trains with an expected total production capacity of approximately 5 mtpa of LNG (the “CCL Midscale Trains 8 & 9 Project”), inclusive of estimated debottlenecking opportunities.

Cheniere is also pursuing liquefaction expansion opportunities and other projects along the LNG value chain. Cheniere is headquartered in Houston, Texas, and has additional offices in London, Singapore, Beijing, Tokyo, Dubai and Washington, D.C.
